parsed.explanation: Combined regime: no documented traveller-facing border friction for foreign-document holders, but the dossier documents state-directed custody harm. Since 2022 arbitrary mass raids have captured trans women, who are held in the ordinary prison system by birth sex with no gender-identity accommodation. The documented case involved forced haircutting, handcuffed squat punishment, and denial of HIV care, and one woman remained imprisoned. Police, soldiers and guards target effeminate men. Medical care is restricted and dismissive. Remedies are weak: one judicial release after four months, and an enhanced hate-crime framework with one documented conviction. Resident-only gaps are weighted lightly. Score sits below the 0.25-C anchor and above the 0.15-B anchor.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border or entry-screening action against foreign-document trans visitors. Lack of domestic gender-recognition is resident-facing and not treated as visitor exposure.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor documents are not documented as checked against domestic rules, so exposure rests on later arrest and custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans women arbitrarily captured in mass raids since March 2022 are held in ordinary prisons by birth sex with no accommodation. Documented abuse includes forced haircutting, punishment drills and denial of HIV clinic access. Police lockup precedes prison.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: A judge freed one woman after about four months, finding the arrest unsupported. The other woman remained imprisoned.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Raids combine state targeting with birth-sex placement. A visitor caught in a raid faces the same custody regime, and release depends on judicial review that is slow.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National prison system places trans women by birth sex. Prison rules forbid effeminate dress for homosexual inmates, and guards target effeminate men.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Custody placement is national, so no local variation offers relief.

care_services.exposure: Hospital specialists dismiss trans problems, patients wait longer or are denied care, and hormone and surgical protocols are lacking. Patients distrust the system after surgical side effects.
care_services.protection: A 2009 health ministry guideline bans discrimination against LGBT people in health services, but operation is not documented.
care_services.interaction: Care denial is compounded when a detained trans person is refused HIV clinic access.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State officers target trans women and effeminate men through raids, unwarranted searches, theft and sexual assault. Police refused to cooperate in LGBT death investigations.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The 2015 enhanced hate-crime penalty (30 to 60 years) and the 2015 hate-crime provisions are on the books.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Enforcement of the hostile raids is state-run, while the hate-crime framework has one documented conviction.

minors_guardians.exposure: Dossier documents family conversion therapy and expulsion of LGBT children, and school expulsion. It is resident-facing and does not describe travelling minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor in custody would face birth-sex placement with the same adult custody regime. No minor-specific rule is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: About 500 anti-LGBT hate crimes reported 1998 to 2015, many unreported. Gang physical and sexual assault and extortion of LGBT people. A 2013 study found 85% considered attacks on trans people acceptable.
street_violence_police_response.protection: The first homicide conviction (2020) of police officers for killing a trans woman, with 20-year sentences. Prosecution of a hate-crime death.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Public hostility is compounded by police involvement in abuse. Convictions are isolated and the 2013 attitude figure is dated.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Human-rights reports find failure to address violence and discrimination. Obstacles to protection are documented. Complaints under the 2018 policy have no sourced outcomes.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have ordered reform (2022 name-law ruling, not enacted as of 2023) and freed at least one wrongly detained woman.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Judicial relief exists but is slow and selective, and the legislature has not implemented rulings.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both have birth-sex prison housing with assaults and a cross-dressing arrest route. This case adds documented state raids targeting trans women and specific abuse (forced haircutting, punishment drills, HIV care denial). It lacks the 0.25-C capital-prohibition record. Judged slightly lower.

Both involve detention, assaults and withheld care. This case has no documented habeas-driven punishment of complainants and no documented deaths in custody, and does include a judicial release. Judged higher.

Both involve state targeting and lengthy detention. 0.35-B documents release after hours and no imprisonment. This case documents months-long imprisonment, birth-sex placement and custodial abuse. Judged lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative exposure is state custody. Mass raids targeting trans women route them into birth-sex prison housing with documented abuse and delayed, selective judicial release. Care is denied in detention and restricted in hospitals. Protections (hate-crime penalties, the police homicide conviction, the 2022 name-law ruling) are either isolated or unimplemented. Resident-only gaps are weighted lightly. The result is a high-risk band rating.
